text:
alana: Heads-up — sales asked for a P95=120ms SLA for Nimbus, but the current runtime profile shows a widening P99 tail when we enable the quantized kernel. Can we sketch options by EOD?

matt: Ack. I saw the perf regression in the canary run. P50/P95 look fine, P99 jumps ~2.5x for sequences >512. Likely kernel path + KV miss amplification.

sophia: Quick data point: last profiling session (profile id 202103) shows microbatch=8 has lower median but worse tail compared to microbatch=4. Might be due to interleaved attention kernel hitting worst-case memory.

alana: Sales wants a single number to offer customers. Product_jane thinking p95 is what marketing asks for, sales_omar wants p99 for enterprise deals. We need a pragmatic carveout.

product_jane: I don't want us to overpromise. For PLG tiers we can say p95 default, enterprise add p99 SLA as premium. But need engineering proof it won’t blow up cost.

sales_omar: Customer (FinCorp) literally asked for p99=200ms at 50 qps sustained. They’ll pay for reserved capacity, but we need clear tradeoffs — microbatch config, canary plan, fallback model.

matt: Proposal: offer p95=120ms on shared pool, enterprise reserved config for p99=200ms with: microbatch=4, kv_warmup=enabled, kernel_variant=stable64, pre-warmed KV shards=2. That lets us avoid quant kernel tail.

sophia: Agreed but note this increases GPU cost ~22% in our sim. Also ops complexity: warmup traffic, KV preheat window 30s.

alana: Can we show a quick config snippet for sales to include?

matt: Sure — example policy they can sign off on:

```json
{
  "slo": {"p95_ms": 120, "p99_ms": 200},
  "deployment": "reserved",
  "microbatch": 4,
  "kv": {"warmup": true, "prewarmed_shards": 2, "ttl_ms": 60000},
  "kernel": "stable64",
  "canary": {"enabled": true, "traffic": "5%", "duration_min": 30}
}
```

infra_bot: deploy.bot: Canary started for release r2021-11 on pool reserved-nimbus-01 (5% traffic).

product_jane: Good. Also include fallback policy: if P99 breach >3x in 10m then automatic fallback to fallback_model=v0.9 and route to lower quant variant.

matt: Right, fallback threshold and alerting. Also recommend continuous KV hit-rate monitor. If hits drop <80% within 2m we scale prewarm or reduce microbatch.

sophia: One more nuance: for long sequences (>1024) we should prefer kernel_variant=attention-tiling which exhibits better tail despite slightly higher median. Should we include sequence-length routing?

alana: Sequence-length routing adds complexity but could be a win for FinCorp. Sales ok with a small ranger fee for custom routing?

sales_omar: They will accept a small premium. Ask legal to add the routing clause.

alana: Action items: 1) Matt validate cost delta with microbatch=4 vs 8 and produce numbers (due tomorrow). 2) Sophia run a 2-hour KV-warmup canary to validate tail under sustained 50 qps (due tomorrow). 3) Product craft SLA wording (p95 default, p99 reserved) and fallback clause (due EOD). 4) Infra to build canary hook and alerting (infra_bot noted).

matt: Will run cost sims — preliminary estimate +22% GPU, +5% infra (KV prewarm) for p99 carveout.

sophia: Starting the KV-warmup canary now. I'll post results in this thread when ready.

infra_bot: deploy.bot: Canary completed (30m). Observed P99 spike at minute 17 — root cause: kernel swap triggered by dynamic quant path. Rolling rollback to stable64 succeeded.

alana: Thanks — can someone capture the regression repro steps? We need an RCA to include with product note.

matt: Repro steps: 1) enable quantized kernel. 2) traffic spike with seq>512 + microbatch=8. 3) KV miss rate rises -> more KV fetchs -> memory pressure -> kernel fall back to slower path. Attaching heap traces to the incident ticket.

product_jane: OK — given that, we’ll recommend stable64 + prewarm for p99 SLAs and keep quant kernel as opt-in. That keeps tail predictable.

sales_omar: I'll tell FinCorp engineering that p99=200ms is achievable on reserved with the listed config and will flag the opt-in quant as "experimental".

alana: Great. Closing loop: Matt & Sophia post updates tomorrow, product will finalize wording. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

sophia: Posting initial KV canary summary: avg P95=115ms, P99=180ms after prewarm, cost up ~24% vs baseline. Details in the ticket.

matt: Updated cost sims attached. If legal wants a carveout we can add a warmup window clause (30s) before SLA enforcement.

alana: Perfect. We'll re-open if anything changes.
